definitions.explanation: The spread of cancer or disease from one part of the body to another. The most common usage in everyday Japanese.
A shift or transfer from one state, position, or condition to another. Used in academic, scientific, and general contexts.

examples.japanese: がんが{肺|はい}に{転移|てんい}した。
examples.english: The cancer spread to the lungs.

examples.japanese: {早期|そうき}{発見|はっけん}なら{転移|てんい}を{防|ふせ}げる{可能性|かのうせい}がある。
examples.english: If detected early, there is a possibility of preventing metastasis.

examples.japanese: {検査|けんさ}の{結果|けっか}、{他|ほか}の{臓器|ぞうき}への{転移|てんい}は{見|み}られなかった。
examples.english: The examination results showed no metastasis to other organs.

examples.japanese: {関心|かんしん}が{別|べつ}の{話題|わだい}に{転移|てんい}した。
examples.english: Interest shifted to a different topic.

examples.japanese: {相|そう}{転移|てんい}は{物理学|ぶつりがく}の{重要|じゅうよう}なテーマだ。
examples.english: Phase transitions are an important topic in physics.

examples.japanese: {権力|けんりょく}の{転移|てんい}が{平和|へいわ}に{行|おこな}われることが{民主主義|みんしゅしゅぎ}の{基本|きほん}だ。
examples.english: The peaceful transfer of power is fundamental to democracy.

notes:
{転移|てんい} is a noun that can function as a suru verb ({転移|てんい}する).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- がんの{転移|てんい} (cancer metastasis)
- {遠隔|えんかく}{転移|てんい} (distant metastasis)
- {相|そう}{転移|てんい} (phase transition)
- {権力|けんりょく}の{転移|てんい} (transfer of power)

In medical contexts, {転移|てんい} almost always refers to the spread of cancer. The compound {転移|てんい}がん (metastatic cancer) is also common. In physics, {相|そう}{転移|てんい} (phase transition) is a standard technical term.
